correctness.rationale: For uniform n-point circular spacings, a graph is connected unless at least two gaps exceed r, hence K=max(1,H), while each isolated vertex corresponds exactly to two adjacent long gaps. With E_i independent Exp(1), gaps E_i/S_n, t_n=nr_n=(log n+x)/2, the fixed-threshold binomial exceedance B has mean c sqrt(n) and variance asymptotic c sqrt(n), with normalized CLT. The random-threshold discrepancy is O_P(log n)=o_P(n^(1/4)), via |S_n−n|=O_P(sqrt(n)); thus K has the stated Gaussian limit. Given H=h long gaps, long-gap locations are uniform and the kth falling factorial moment of singleton vertices is (h)_k(h−1)_k/(n−1)_k, tending c^(2k) when h/sqrt(n)→c. Conditional Poisson and unconditional Gaussian therefore decouple. Dirichlet simplex gives a_j=(1−jr)_+^(n−1); E[HI]=2n a2+n(n−2)a3, E[H]=n a1, E[I]=n a2 and Cov(K,I)=Cov(H,I)−P(H=0)E I→2c². Independent exact evaluation at x=0 for n=100,1000,10000,100000 showed covariance 0.714,1.168,1.551,1.783 approaching 2. This convergence experiment does not prove the limit; analytic expansion does.
